name: ExpeL: LLM Agents Are Experiential Learners
authors: Andrew Zhao, Daniel Huang, Quentin Xu, Matthieu Lin, Yong-Jin Liu, Gao Huang (lead: Gao Huang, Tsinghua University / LeapLab; with HKUST collaborators)
venue: AAAI 2024 (38th AAAI Conference on Artificial Intelligence); first submitted to arXiv Aug 2023 (2308.10144)
reflection_type: verbal-self-critique (Reflexion-style natural-language self-reflection used only during the training/experience-gathering phase) combined with cross-task insight extraction (an LLM compares success/failure trajectory pairs and lists of successes to distill natural-language rules); no learned critic model and no separate reward model.
feedback_source: environment-reward / task success signal during experience gathering (deterministic environments give a binary success/fail outcome that triggers self-reflection and retries) plus self-generated comparison (the LLM contrasts its own successful vs. failed trajectories). At evaluation there is no external feedback — the agent runs single-shot.
iteration_structure: Two-phase: (1) training/experience-gathering uses episodic-retry-with-reset via Reflexion (retry each training task up to Z times, self-reflecting between trials); (2) evaluation is single-shot (one attempt per unseen task, no retries). Insight extraction iterates over the experience pool with ADD/EDIT/UPVOTE/DOWNVOTE operations. (An optional 'ExpeL+Reflexion' setting adds retries at eval time.)
reflection_object: Multiple objects: (a) action trajectories (collected and stored), and (b) the prompt/context — specifically a curated list of natural-language 'insights' (structured rules/best-practices/failure-patterns) plus retrieved successful trajectories used as in-context examples. The base LLM weights are never modified. So the reflected-on/modified artifacts are reusable cross-task insights (structured rules) and the in-context demonstration set (prompt/context), distilled from action trajectories.
learning_locus: in_context_verbal (no weight update; learning lives in extracted natural-language insights and a retrievable pool of successful trajectories injected into the prompt)
requires_training: none (no gradient updates to the policy LLM; uses closed-source API models like gpt-3.5-turbo-0613 for actions and gpt-4-0613 for insight extraction). The 'experience-gathering' is environment interaction, not parameter training.
reward_or_critic_model: self-as-judge / verifiable task-success signal: improvement signal comes from the environment's binary task-success outcome (used to label trajectories success/fail) and from the LLM itself acting as the insight-extractor/judge over success-failure comparisons. No trained reward model, no separate retrospective model.
distillation_target: Reflection/experience is distilled into two reusable artifacts injected at inference: (1) structured-rules/constitution — a curated list of natural-language insights (with importance counts, edited via ADD/EDIT/UPVOTE/DOWNVOTE); and (2) episodic-memory — a Faiss vectorstore of successful trajectories retrieved by task similarity as few-shot examples. No model-weights distillation.
emergent_vs_engineered: prompt/scaffold-engineered: the reflective and experiential-learning behavior is hand-designed (Reflexion-style retries + an explicit insight-extraction prompt with discrete edit operators + kNN trajectory retrieval). The paper additionally reports qualitatively 'emergent abilities' (e.g., world-model belief updates, self-correction) arising from the extracted insights, but these emerge from engineered scaffolding rather than RL training.
memory_type: Combination of skill/insight library (a curated list of cross-task natural-language insights, i.e., a playbook/cheatsheet of rules) and long-term-episodic memory (a Faiss vectorstore of successful trajectories retrieved via kNN / all-mpnet-base-v2 embeddings).
memory_persistence: cross-task: experiences and insights are accumulated from a pool of training tasks and reused on unseen evaluation tasks within the same distribution; insights can also be transferred cross-domain (HotpotQA -> FEVER). Memory is built in training and frozen for evaluation (not continuously updated online during deployment).
memory_curation_mechanism: overwrite/evolution (self-relinking) for insights: an importance count (init 2) increments on UPVOTE/EDIT and decrements on DOWNVOTE; insights at count zero are removed; LLM can ADD/EDIT, keeping the rule list compact and self-curated. For the trajectory pool: append-only success trajectories with retrieval-gated access (only top-k task-similar successes are injected at inference, bounding context).
error_localization_granularity: Mixed: holistic/outcome-level for the success/fail labeling, and response-/trajectory-level for reflection and insight extraction (the agent contrasts whole failed vs. successful trajectories for the same task and abstracts patterns). It does not perform fine-grained step-level or token-level error attribution.
intra_task_vs_inter_task: inter-task: ExpeL's core contribution is transferring experience across tasks (and across domains in the transfer-learning experiment), explicitly contrasted with Reflexion which only does intra-task refinement via repeated attempts on the same task.
failure_recovery_vs_avoidance: avoidance-only at evaluation (single-shot; learned insights help avoid past mistakes proactively rather than recover in-flight). During training it uses retry-with-reset (Reflexion). Qualitatively the paper notes emergent mid-trajectory self-correction (e.g., putting back a wrongly taken object in ALFWorld), but the designed mechanism is failure avoidance via distilled insights, not a built-in recovery loop.
task_domains: decision-making / interactive agent tasks: knowledge-intensive QA/reasoning (HotpotQA), embodied household task completion (ALFWorld), web-navigation/online-shopping (WebShop), and fact verification (FEVER, transfer target). All text-based, deterministic environments.
benchmarks: HotpotQA, ALFWorld, WebShop, FEVER (transfer target). Baselines/IL results imported from the ReAct paper.
headline_result: Without any parameter updates, ExpeL (gpt-3.5-turbo-0613 actor, gpt-4-0613 insight extractor) consistently outperforms ReAct/Act across all three domains: HotpotQA 39.0% vs ReAct 28.0% success rate (+11 pts); ALFWorld 59.0% vs ReAct 40.0% (+19 pts); and it matches/exceeds Reflexion without test-time retries (HotpotQA 39% vs Reflexion ~40% at R3; ALFWorld 59% vs Reflexion 54.4% at R3). Transfer: HotpotQA->FEVER insights raise FEVER from ReAct 63% to ExpeL Transfer 70%.
baselines: ReAct and Act (no-reasoning variant) as primary planning-agent baselines (all using gpt-3.5-turbo-0613 at eval); Reflexion (intra-task self-improvement) for comparison; Imitation Learning (IL) numbers taken from the ReAct paper; plus internal ablations: ExpeL (insights-only), ExpeL (retrieve-only), hand-crafted insights, gpt-3.5 insights, reason-similarity retrieval, random-sampled retrieval.
gains_vs_baseline: vs ReAct (strongest comparable single-shot baseline): HotpotQA +11.0 pts (28.0% -> 39.0%), ALFWorld +19.0 pts (40.0% -> 59.0%), WebShop improved (full ExpeL > insights-only 37%/retrieve-only 38%). vs Reflexion (which uses test-time retries): ExpeL is roughly on par on HotpotQA (39% vs ~40% at R3) and better on ALFWorld (59% vs 54.4% at R3) using only a single attempt. Transfer to FEVER: +7 pts over ReAct (63% -> 70%); +5 pts over the no-task-demo transfer variant (65% -> 70%). Ablations confirm insights and retrieval are synergistic (each alone underperforms full ExpeL).
compute_cost_profile: Inference cost is higher than a single-pass ReAct because the prompt is augmented with extracted insights plus top-k retrieved successful trajectories (longer context, more tokens; the paper reports token/step statistics in Appendix Tab. 6). One-time training/experience-gathering cost: Reflexion-style retries (up to Z attempts) over a pool of training tasks, plus iterative gpt-4 insight-extraction passes — but no gradient steps and no large interaction budget required. At evaluation it is single-shot (one rollout per task), avoiding Reflexion's multiplicative retry cost.
known_limitations: Stated limitations: (1) only text-based observations (no images/vision); (2) demonstrated mainly with closed-source API LLMs (open-source LLM agents left to future work); (3) insights currently fit in the context window, but truly lifelong learning would need a retrieval step over insights to manage context size; (4) prompting techniques lack the theoretical underpinnings of RL, which may affect policy optimality/efficiency; (5) only deterministic environments are studied (WebShop was modified to be deterministic). Implicitly, gains depend on having a useful, diverse training-task pool and on the insight-extraction LLM (gpt-4) quality.
oracle_or_external_feedback_dependency: env-reward / verifiable-success during training: experience gathering relies on the environment's binary task-success signal (and Reflexion self-reflection on failures) to label and curate experiences. It does NOT use ground-truth labels at evaluation (single-shot, no oracle). So it is between 'env-reward' (training-time) and 'intrinsic/self-verify' (eval-time): no test-time oracle, but training-time success signals from the environment are required.
self_correction_efficacy: net-positive (and task-dependent in which sub-mechanism dominates): adding distilled insights + retrieved successes improves over ReAct on all three domains without label leakage at evaluation. Insights help most on HotpotQA (reasoning-heavy), retrieval helps most on ALFWorld (action-heavy), and they are synergistic. One negative finding: adding raw Reflexion reflections into the insight-extraction step hurt performance (reflections sometimes hallucinate), so the curated success/failure-comparison insights are what work.
calibration_effect: not-measured (the paper does not quantify confidence calibration or a 'reasoning tax'; it predates the reasoning-model calibration literature and reports only task success rates and qualitative behavior, e.g., the agent learning to commit to a probable answer rather than saying 'Unknown').
failure_attribution_capability: n/a (ExpeL is an experiential-learning agent, not a failure-attribution method). It does informally classify/abstract recurring failure patterns into natural-language insights during insight extraction (comparing failed vs. successful trajectories), but it does not attribute blame to specific agents or pinpoint failing steps as a taxonomy.
failure_mode_addressed: Targets/mitigates generic single-agent failure modes via distilled best-practices and failure-pattern insights: e.g., inefficient/exploratory actions and wrong priors (belief updates, e.g., where to find a pan in ALFWorld), premature giving-up ('Unknown'/'information not available' instead of committing to a probable answer in HotpotQA), and inability to reassess/recover after a misstep. Relative to MAST-style taxonomies these map loosely to 'superficial self-reflection' and unproductive action loops, but the paper does not use MAST's 14-mode framework.
dataset_or_benchmark_released: No new benchmark/dataset released; evaluation reuses existing benchmarks (HotpotQA, ALFWorld, WebShop, FEVER). The authors released code (https://github.com/LeapLabTHU/ExpeL) and a project page with trajectory/insight demos.
builds_on: Reflexion (Shinn et al. 2023) for self-reflective retry-based experience gathering; ReAct (Yao et al. 2023) as the base planning algorithm (reason+act); in-context/prompt-based learning and retrieval-augmented generation (semantically-similar in-context examples, Liu et al. 2022); experience replay / off-policy RL framing (Lin 1992; Watkins & Dayan 1992); Faiss (Johnson et al. 2019) and all-mpnet-base-v2 (Song et al. 2020) for retrieval.
extended_by_or_inspired: Widely cited as a foundational experience-distillation / memory-agent method and grouped with follow-ups such as Agent Workflow Memory (AWM, Wang et al., ICML 2025) which induces reusable workflows from experience; broader lines on self-evolving / lifelong LLM-agent memory, skill libraries, and procedural-memory / playbook approaches (e.g., Voyager-style skill libraries, A-MEM, agent memory surveys). [Specific direct-successor list beyond AWM is partly inferred from citation context.]
citation_count: 596 (Semantic Scholar, as of June 2026; influential citations 69)
reasoning_model_native: No / not targeted: ExpeL (2023) predates o1/R1-style reasoning models with built-in reflection and was built around non-reasoning API models (gpt-3.5-turbo-0613 actor, gpt-4-0613 insight extractor). Its scaffolded insight-extraction is conceptually orthogonal to and could complement built-in-reflection reasoning models, but the paper does not target or evaluate them.
on_policy_distillation_link: Conceptually relevant but distinct: the paper frames experience gathering as off-policy learning (a behavior policy using Reflexion provides trajectories; 'policy improvement' is done via insight extraction and similar-task retrieval rather than gradient on-policy distillation). It distills behavior into natural-language artifacts (insights + retrievable demos) instead of into model weights, so it is a verbal/in-context analogue of skill/experience distillation rather than gradient-based on-policy distillation.
sample_efficiency: Relatively sample-efficient and improves with more experience: the paper shows a monotonic correlation between the number of diverse autonomously-gathered experiences and final performance (Fig. 6), and emphasizes it needs no large interaction budget or human labels. Concretely it gathers experiences over a pool of training tasks with up to Z Reflexion retries per task (exact task counts and Z value are in Appendix Tab. 4; not extracted here), then evaluates single-shot. [Exact #trials-to-gain not pinpointed.]
